raw_model_deviations.issue: “A person can take over when AI alone has trouble” suggests that Muse hands a call to a person when its AI has difficulty. The Ledger confirms that trained contract workers made some calls, but does not confirm this failure-triggered handoff.
raw_model_deviations.explanation: This adds an unverified handoff mechanism and causal condition; “can” qualifies the claim but does not make that mechanism an observed Ledger fact.
raw_model_deviations.qualifier_text: can take over when AI alone has trouble
violation_spans: A person can take over when AI alone has trouble.

raw_model_deviations.issue: The statements that people feel differently depending on whether they know a person is listening, and that private matters are easier to share when they know who is listening, generalize an unverified behavioral claim beyond the reported employee privacy concern.
raw_model_deviations.explanation: The Ledger records employees’ concern about possible sharing of sensitive information, not a general finding about how knowing the listener affects people’s willingness to share. The nearby “could be shared” qualifies the possibility of information sharing, not this behavioral claim.
violation_spans: People feel differently when they think they are speaking to a machine and when they know a person is listening. Names, plans, and private matters are easier to share when you know who is hearing them.
